analyzed_vuln.description: GetMagickByteBufferDatum compacts/refills the fixed 8192-byte stack buffer using all remaining capacity, but never reserves space for or writes a NUL terminator before returning `buffer->data+1` as a `char *`. ReadPSInfo then passes this non-terminated datum to GlobExpression at coders/ps.c:344-346. GlobExpression treats it as an unbounded C/UTF-8 string, advances through the buffer, and GetNextUTFCode ultimately reads past the end of the stack-resident `MagickByteBuffer::data`. The patch should ensure the returned datum is always terminated (reserve one byte and set it), rather than merely changing the crashing UTF decoder.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: A PS/EPS input must reach ReadPSInfo and contain a DSC `DocumentProcessColors:` marker at a buffer position that causes GetMagickByteBufferDatum to compact/refill attacker bytes. The resulting datum must lack an in-buffer NUL through the end of the 8192-byte data array, and a searched token must be absent long enough for GlobExpression to scan to that end. In this PoV, repeated nonzero data includes `DocumentProcessColors:` followed by misspelled `Cny` (so the first `*Cyan*` search fails across the buffer), with non-ASCII bytes also decoded along the way; the unbounded scan reaches the stack-buffer boundary and GetNextUTFCode performs the out-of-bounds byte read.

args: In imagemagick/coders/bytebuffer-private.h, what is the safest minimal root-cause fix for GetMagickByteBufferDatum() so its returned char pointer is always NUL-terminated while preserving byte-buffer stream behavior? Please analyze invariants on i, offset, and count, whether sizeof(data)-i-1 can underflow, and whether ReadMagickByteBuffer also needs to reserve a byte. If this corresponds to a known upstream ImageMagick fix, provide its exact shape.

The ASan report shows a stack-buffer-overflow in GetNextUTFCode called by GlobExpression from ReadPSInfo at imagemagick/coders/ps.c lines 340-346. GetMagickByteBufferDatum in imagemagick/coders/bytebuffer-private.h currently starts i=1, compacts remaining bytes from offset through count, then calls ReadBlob with sizeof(buffer->data)-i, adds i to count, sets offset=1, and returns data+1 without writing a terminator. The organizer explicitly says the correct patch must reserve one byte and set it, rather than changing UTF decoding. The data array is 8192 bytes. Calls generally happen after parser bytes have been consumed, but I want to avoid unsigned underflow or silently dropping buffered input in edge cases.
